source_read: PDF pp. 1-13 (PDFs/MDMA/Brett_2025_MDMAATSystematicReview.pdf): text extraction and rendered pp. 2, 3, 4, 7, 8 and 9 for paragraphs and Tables 1-5. Trial values checked against the MAPP1 and MAPP2 publisher pages and registry records, and the retraction grounds against the three Psychopharmacology notices, all read in my own browser tab. Step 1 not run this round.

design.note: Systematic review without meta-analysis (tabulation and vote counting); AMSTAR 2 is the right instrument.

key_findings.note: Methods, p. 2 (one paragraph). The finding leaves out the search keywords: breakthrough therapy, MDMA, PTSD, post-traumatic stress disorder, MDMA-AT and MAPS, with no Boolean combination given (see missed).
p. 2, Results › Study and participant characteristics, 1st paragraph, and the Table 1 footnote (MP4, NCT01958593).
Recomputed from Table 1: active arms 12 + 8 + 22 + 19 + 46 + 53 = 160; control arms 8 + 4 + 6 + 7 + 44 + 51 = 120.
The phase 3 placebo results the table omits are 12/37 (32%) for MAPP1 and 20/42 (47.6%) for MAPP2, checked in the trial reports.

key_findings.correction: The MAPP2 rows of Table 3 are MAPP2's Table 2 with rounded percentages, except that feeling cold (11 vs 3) is missing; the MAPP1 rows cannot be traced to the article, whose counts are only in an unread supplement, and differ from the registry (muscle tightness 29 vs 5 against 28 vs 6; see reporting issue 5). The rest of the finding (reporting varied; muscle tightness or jaw clenching in the top three in all six trials; headache most common on placebo) is right.

key_findings.note: The note's 4 vs 7 is right for treatment discontinuation, but the review's four per arm matches the participants without an 18-week assessment (see reporting issue 3).
p. 9, the 2nd paragraph starting on that page; no citation in it.

reporting_issues.note: MAPP2 placebo 20/42 (47.6%) checked in MAPP2's Results › Exploratory outcomes, 1st paragraph.

Table 5 gives 95% (participants, 2011 pilot), 58.1% and 72.7% (Ot'alora), none for MAPP1 and 94.2% for MAPP2. The 90% lower bound equals 100% minus MAPP1's 'at least 10%' wrong guesses, which is an upper bound on correct guesses, not a rate; the review does not say so, but nothing else in its tables gives 90%.

Not a transcription error: the review's four per arm matches MAPP1's Fig. 1b count of participants without an 18-week (T4) assessment (42 of 46 and 40 of 44 completed it, three placebo participants having given off-treatment values). Treatment discontinuation was 4 vs 7, so the consequence stands; and for MAPP2 the review counts treatment discontinuation (1 vs 8), so its two phase 3 figures measure different things.
Checked against MAPP1's Table 2 and MAPP2's Results › Safety, 5th paragraph (13/53 and 12/51 at the final preparation session, V4); the 15/104 baseline is not in MAPP2's main text.
Registry 28/46 vs 6/44; the review's 4 (5%) rows are intrusive thoughts, vomiting, stress and musculoskeletal pain.

Table 2 is itself inconsistent for Ot'alora et al. (2018): its efficacy column gives the active placebo as 40 mg and its clinical-response column as 30 mg, while Table 1 gives 40 mg (30 mg is the active placebo of Mithoefer et al., 2018). The other points (the 40 mg threshold for the 160; phase 3 listed by the first session's initial dose only; 80-120 mg in the Appendix) are right.
Table 2: the 100% is 7/7 at 2 months (2011 pilot).

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial. The quotation on unblinding is verbatim (p. 9, 12 words) and has no source; the main conclusion cites the retracted Mithoefer et al. (2019) (p. 8).

missed: The search keywords included 'Multidisciplinary Association for Psychedelic Studies (MAPS)' and 'breakthrough therapy' (Methods, p. 2), and how they were combined is not reported. If combined with AND, the search could only return MAPS-linked papers. The card's selection_effects and where_it_stands ('found no randomized trial ... without a link to MAPS'), and the evidence_no of cl_mdma_therapy_contested, read this as an absence of independent trials; it may partly reflect the search.
The rerun is called 'the same exact search'; with the 2002-2022 limit kept it could not have found MAPP2 (2023), so its date limits must have changed and are not reported.

The review's account of the retractions (data from a site where a serious ethical violation occurred, p. 2; 'publicly documented on YouTube', p. 9, unsourced) leaves out both grounds the notices give: that the authors knew of the MP4 violations at submission and neither disclosed them nor removed that site's data, and that competing interests were not fully declared (checked on the three notices). The card should not cite the review for the grounds.
